annotation.authors_or_issuer: Yoon, H.; Kim, M.-G.; Park, C.; Ahn, H.-N.
key_provisions_or_claims: Service preferences of exhibition visitors form three dimensions: proactive support, adaptive responsiveness, autonomy-oriented minimal service.
Hedonic motivation influences service preference partly via need for proactive support (mediation).
Cost-sensitive threshold tau = CFP/(CFN+CFP) makes robots intervene only with high confidence.
Logistic regression classified visitor types with ~95.8% accuracy in cross-validation.
Robot intelligence includes situational restraint to respect visitor autonomy.
annotation.summary_en: Preprint empirical study of 164 exhibition visitors proposing psychological boundaries as a regulator of openness to service robots. It derives three service-preference dimensions and a cost-sensitive, boundary-aware interaction policy that withholds proactive intervention unless confidence is high, respecting visitor autonomy. It is a design/HRI paper, not a governance instrument.
annotation.title_clean: Navigating Psychological Boundaries: A Boundary-Aware Interaction Policy for Adaptive Service Robots in Exhibitions
annotation.title_en: Navigating Psychological Boundaries: A Boundary-Aware Interaction Policy for Adaptive Service Robots in Exhibitions
